simple.meaning: רוּשׁ (rûwsh) is a Hebrew action word meaning “to be destitute.” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 24 times in 1 Samuel, 2 Samuel, Psalms, Proverbs, Ecclesiastes, beginning at 1 Samuel 18:23. The surrounding contexts include family, family line, flock, Torah, kingship, city.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to רוּשׁ (H7326) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: רוּשׁ (rûwsh) / H7326 is traced through 1 Samuel 18:23, 2 Samuel 12:1, 2 Samuel 12:3, 2 Samuel 12:4 with source-language evidence and verse context.

timeline.evidenceText: Saul’s servants spoke those words in the ears of David. David said, “Does it seem to you a light thing to be the king’s son-in-law, since I am a poor man, and little known?”
Yahweh sent Nathan to David. He came to him, and said to him, “There were two men in one city; the one rich, and the other poor.

but the poor man had nothing, except one little ewe lamb, which he had bought and raised. It grew up together with him, and with his children. It ate of his own food, drank of his own cup, and lay in his bosom, and was like a daughter to him.

A traveler came to the rich man, and he spared to take of his own flock and of his own herd, to prepare for the wayfaring man who had come to him, but took the poor man’s lamb, and prepared it for the man who had come to him.”
Come, you children, listen to me.
“Defend the weak, the poor, and the fatherless.
He becomes poor who works with a lazy hand,
There are some who pretend to be rich, yet have nothing.
The ransom of a man’s life is his riches,
An abundance of food is in poor people’s fields,
The poor person is shunned even by his own neighbor,
Whoever mocks the poor reproaches his Maker.
The poor plead for mercy,
Better is the poor who walks in his integrity
All the relatives of the poor shun him:
That which makes a man to be desired is his kindness.
The rich and the poor have this in common:
The rich rule over the poor.
A needy man who oppresses the poor
Better is the poor who walks in his integrity,

definitions.full: H7326. rush רָאשׁ poor , רֵאשׁ poverty , see רושׁ . [ רוּשׁ or רִישׁ ] 24 verb be in want, poor (related to ירשׁ [compare Qal 3, Niph`al Hiph`il 3 ]? so Thes); — Qal Perfect 3plural וְרָעֵ֑בוּ רָשׁוּ כְּפִירִים Psa 34:11 young lions are in want and hunger ; elsewhere Participle רָשׁ 1Sam 18:23 16 t., רָאשׁ 2Sam 12:1-2 t.; plural רָשִׁים Prov 22:7 , רָאשִׁים 13:23 ; — (often opposed to עָשִׁיר ): as adjective 1Sam 18:23 ; 2Sam 12:1 , 4 ; Prov 28:3 ; Eccl 4:14 ; as substantive = poor man ( men ), 2Sam 12:3 ; Psa 82:3 ; Eccl 5:7 , especially Prov 10:4 ; 13:8 , 23 12 t. Proverbs. Hithpo`lel Participle מִתְרוֺשֵׁשׁ Prov 13:7 one impoverishing himself (opposed to מִתְעַשֵּׁר ; compare Pô'l. רושׁשׁ Ecclus 11:12; Ecclus 13:5). — Jer 5:17 ; Mal 1:4 see רשׁשׁ . p. 439f
